category: German multihoster selling prepaid traffic packages with unmetered usenet

free_tier.stated: No free traffic on this tariff; it is the second paid level. The free tariff is a separate record.

per_object_cap.stated: not stated: there is no per-file ceiling, only a traffic balance for filehoster traffic

retention.stated: Packages expire with their term - '1 Monat' is 30 days (720 hours) - and unused traffic is lost unless the '_Keep' option moves it into a new package of the same tariff and an equal or longer term

egress.terms: Same prepaid traffic model as Premium, with one material difference: 'Usenet ohne Trafficanrechnung' and 'TV ohne Trafficanrechnung' - usenet and TV-recorder traffic are not charged against the package at all. Filehoster traffic still is.
egress.free_allowance: package volume for filehosters; usenet unmetered
egress.price_per_tb: EUR 15.99 per TB for 30 days at the 750 GB package

interface_detail: JSON API at high-way.me/api/ plus WebDAV, FTP and SFTP; usenet access is issued as standard NNTP credentials with 20 connections.
tooling: API, WebDAV/FTP/SFTP, NNTP clients, JDownloader, pyLoad, Android TV app.
chaining: The interesting combination is unmetered usenet on top of a metered filehoster balance: a client can pull a terabyte from usenet here without touching the package, which no other service offers at any price.

limits.value: 250 GB / 500 GB / 750 GB per 30 days at EUR 9.99 / 10.99 / 11.99; 3 TB per year at EUR 71.99 - and only for filehoster traffic
unused traffic expires with the term; only the _Keep option carries it into a new package
usenet with 20 connections, the highest of the three tariffs
vetted registration, review takes a few hours

limits_note: Despite the name, the filehoster side is fully metered and capped by the package; 'Unlimited' refers to usenet and TV not being charged. That is the misreading this record exists to prevent.
binding_note: Filehoster bytes are counted, so the package size is the constraint, and it is a worse EUR-per-TB than Premium at every volume (EUR 15.99 vs EUR 12.00 per TB at 750 GB). A client whose 1 TiB month comes from usenet is unaffected; one that comes from filehosters pays more for the same bytes than on the Premium tariff.

identity_cost.detail: E-mail registration plus manual review and a forum account; payment by card, PaysafeCard or Amazon coupon.

reliability_note: Unmetered usenet is the only part not counted; filehoster traffic expires with the term and is billed at up to the full file size when a download manager uses multiple connections.
confidence_note: Package prices, the usenet exemption, connection counts and expiry rules all come from vendor pages read. Whether the tariff page's 'ab mtl. EUR 5,99' is included in the package price is not stated anywhere reachable, so no combined figure is recorded.

evidence.proved: the UNLIMITED package ladder: 1 month 250 GB EUR 9.99, 500 GB EUR 10.99, 750 GB EUR 11.99; 1 year 3 TB EUR 71.99; 2 years 6 TB EUR 143.99
'UNLIMITED, ab mtl. € 5,99', 'Usenet mit 20 Verbindungen', 'Usenet ohne Trafficanrechnung', 'TV ohne Trafficanrechnung'
the 30-day month definition, package expiry, and the _Keep rules for carrying traffic into a new package

price_per_tb_month: EUR 15.99 per TB per 30 days at 750 GB for EUR 11.99; EUR 24.00 per TB at 3 TB for one year (EUR 71.99); usenet unmetered
notes: At that volume the effective rate is EUR 39.96 a TB, the worst, and the tier only becomes sensible when usenet carries the bulk. The name is the trap and the vendor's own footnote contradicts it: filehoster traffic is charged.
